caption:
Office card coming? AI writes your line. Ask it for 3 short, warm lines, then pick the one that sounds like you.

WHY IT WORKS: a blank card is hard because you have to invent something from nothing. Give AI two facts (a first name and what they do) and it hands you options to react to. Choosing is much easier than starting cold.

THE REAL TEST: we made up a coworker, Dana from accounting, and asked Claude (Anthropic) on Oct 28, 2026: "I have to sign a birthday card for a coworker I barely know. Her name is Dana and she works in accounting. Give me 3 short, warm lines I could write. Nothing cheesy."
Its 3 lines, word for word:
1. "Happy birthday, Dana! Hope your year ahead is a good one, and that it balances out in your favour."
2. "Wishing you a relaxing birthday and a great year ahead. Thanks for everything you do to keep us all on track!"
3. "Happy birthday, Dana! I hope today brings you some well-earned time off from the spreadsheets."
It added: "If you want to keep it simplest, #2 works for anyone, even if you've never really talked."

HOW (about 30 seconds):
1. Open ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini.
2. Type: "I have to sign a birthday card for a coworker I barely know. Her name is [first name] and she works in [team]. Give me 3 short, warm lines I could write. Nothing cheesy."
3. Pick one, change a word so it sounds like you, and write it in by hand.

THE CATCH: AI doesn't know the person, so the lines are friendly but general. If you know one real thing about them (a new dog, a big trip), add it to the prompt.

PRIVACY TIP: a first name and a team is all it needs. Leave out their last name, age, birthday date and anything personal.

caption:
Party in an hour and no costume? List what's in your closet and ask AI for 3 costumes you can make from just those things.

WHY IT WORKS: you know what you own, but not what it adds up to. AI is good at recombining a list, so "striped T-shirt, black jeans, beanie" becomes a character in seconds.

THE REAL TEST: we made up a closet and asked Claude (Anthropic) on Oct 28, 2026: "Halloween party in an hour and I have no costume. Here's what I own: a white bedsheet, a black turtleneck, black jeans, a denim jacket, a red bandana, sunglasses, a striped T-shirt, a beanie, some cardboard and a black marker. Give me 3 costume ideas I can make from just these things, and what to wear for each. Keep it short."
Its 3 ideas: 1. Classic Ghost, 2. Steve Jobs, 3. Cartoon Burglar / Robber. The Reel shows 1 and 3, quoted exactly:
Ghost: "Add the sunglasses over the eye holes if you want a "cool ghost.""
Burglar: "Striped T-shirt, black jeans and the beanie." "Red bandana over your lower face, plus sunglasses."

HOW (2 minutes):
1. Open ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini.
2. List what you own: clothes, accessories, and craft stuff like cardboard, tape or a marker.
3. Ask: "Give me 3 costume ideas I can make from just these things, and what to wear for each. Keep it short." Say how long you have.

THE CATCH: it only knows what you list and can't see your clothes, so try the pieces on before you go. And ask before you cut eye holes in a good sheet.

PRIVACY TIP: a list of clothes is safe to paste. You don't need to upload photos of yourself or your room.

caption:
Dad says he needs nothing? Tell AI what he loves and your budget, and ask for 5 gift ideas, one line each.

AI, for real · Day 11. One real test of what AI can do, with the output shown.

WHY IT WORKS: "he has everything" is a blank page. AI connects what he already enjoys (gardening, crosswords, black coffee) to things at your price, so you start from a short list instead of an endless shopping page.

THE REAL TEST (Dad is made up for this post):
Prompt: "Help me pick a gift for my dad. He's 64, loves gardening and crossword puzzles, drinks his coffee black, and says he doesn't need anything. My budget is $40. Give me 5 ideas, one line each."
Claude's 5 ideas (headings and prices word for word; it added a short reason to each):
1. Premium whole-bean coffee sampler (~$30)
2. Quality garden pruners (~$35)
3. New York Times crossword book plus a nice pen (~$25)
4. Heirloom seed collection (~$25)
5. Personalized garden kneeler or stool (~$40)
Its top pick, word for word: "For a "doesn't need anything" dad, the seeds or the coffee usually work best, because they get used up and won't add clutter."

THE CATCH: the prices are AI estimates, not live prices, and it can't check what's in stock near you. Check the price where you'd actually buy it.

PRIVACY TIP: their likes and your budget are all it needs. Leave out full names, addresses and health details.

Do this: in ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini, type "Help me pick a gift for my dad. He's 64, loves gardening and crossword puzzles, drinks his coffee black, and says he doesn't need anything. My budget is $40. Give me 5 ideas, one line each." Change the person, age, likes and budget to yours.
